Subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool expansion + staged ephemeral fallback (term amendment)

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the productive conversation last week. Per our renewal planning, I wanted to put a concise proposal on the table so your procurement and engineering teams can align:

Summary proposal (high level)
- Reserved capacity: increase NovaApps dedicated pool from 32 -> 56 GPUs (A100 equivalent) across a 12‑month renewal term.
- Throughput target: baseline committed throughput of 3,000 tokens/sec aggregate for the pool, with a 99.5% latency availability SLA on the pinned model family.
- Burst / overflow approach: staged ephemeral fallback (recommended) — allow on‑demand spillover up to a configurable percentage of committed throughput, metered at on‑demand rates but controlled via pre‑purchased burst credits and auto‑throttles.

Why staged ephemeral fallback vs hard cap
- Preserves customer experience in short spikes (e.g., launch days) while keeping cost predictability via burst credits.
- Avoids hard failures when burst events occur; instead we failover to agreed model variants or ephemeral workers with clear cost/latency tradeoffs.

Key operational controls we propose
- Burst ceiling: default 20% of committed throughput (can be adjusted).
- Pre‑purchased burst credit bucket: sized at renewal (we typically recommend 10% of expected peak tokens) with automated alerting at 50%/75%/90% consumption.
- Auto‑fallback policy: when burst credits are exhausted, requests will route to (1) degraded model variant with lower cost/higher latency, then (2) rate‑limit if configured — we can make this behavior configurable per route.
- Reporting: token-level cost/latency dashboard and monthly burst consumption report.

Attachments: Renewal_Term_Summary_v1.pdf (proposal summary).

Questions for you
1) Is a 20% burst ceiling in line with your operational expectations?
2) Do you prefer burst credits as a one‑time top‑up at renewal or a monthly replenishment option?
3) Any procurement timing constraints we should be aware of (PO, contract window, legal review lead times)?

If helpful, I can loop in Sales Ops to put together a pricing appendix and a DocuSign addendum for the reserved capacity + burst credits. Available times for a 30‑minute call this week: Tue 11/2 9–11am or Thu 11/4 3–5pm PT.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez

Alex —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifying items from procurement and our infra lead (Samir):

1) Pricing mechanics for burst credits — can you give a concrete example: if we buy a burst credit bucket equivalent to X token volume, what is the billable rate once we exceed that bucket? Is there a per‑token surcharge or per‑GPU‑hour?

2) Model preservation — when traffic spills to ephemeral workers / smaller variants, will output quality be comparable? We need to understand if degradation is acceptable (and whether it triggers our internal SLA/incident processes).

3) Billing cadence & PO — we prefer to handle the reserved capacity as a monthly invoice with a PO number; are you able to accept monthly invoices for the reserved portion and a separate monthly reconciliation for burst consumption?

4) Timeline — our quarter closes 11/30; we'd like contracts executed by 11/18 to allow provisioning before year end.

Can you send a short appendix with per‑GPU committed price, recommended burst credit sizing and overage rate examples? If you can share that and the legal addendum, we can accelerate review.

Thanks —

Quick internal note for pricing and legal:

Pricing suggestion (draft for appendix)
- Reserved GPUs: $1,800 / GPU / month (A100 equivalent) for committed capacity when committed for 12 months at current volume (discounted band applied at >=48 GPUs).
- Burst credits: sell in blocks equivalent to 10M tokens per block at $250 / block. Overage after blocks: $0.00003 / token (roughly our on‑demand rate).
- Alternatively we can offer a burst GPU‑hour credit (for customers who prefer GPU‑hour accounting): $12 / GPU‑hour for pre‑purchased credits, $18 / GPU‑hour for ad‑hoc on‑demand usage.

Operational controls we should offer in the addendum
- Burst ceiling configurable at renewal (default 20%).
- Auto‑top‑up option: customer can elect automatic top‑up when bucket hits 25% remaining — requires PO confirmation for additional blocks.
- Fallback sequence written explicitly: dedicated pool -> ephemeral on‑demand workers (same model family quantized variant) -> lower‑capacity model variant -> rate limit.

Attachments: SLA_proposal.xlsx (SLA language + metrics), Renewal_Term_Summary_v2.pdf (updated pricing appendix).

Legal note: please run the attached SLA by Legal — we should include a one‑time credit formula for prolonged availability breaches and a clause that burst credits are non‑refundable but transferable across routes within the account.

If this looks good I can produce a one‑page addendum that Sales Ops can convert to DocuSign.
